subject: mud dauber wasp
title: A Wasp Packs 25 Living, Paralyzed Spiders Into a Mud Tube for One Baby

scenes.text: Inside this mud tube are 25 spiders. All alive. None can move.
The mud dauber wasp built it. One female, hauling mud in her jaws, trip after trip, into a pipe of cells.
Then she hunts. She finds a spider, stings it once, and it goes limp. Not dead. Paralyzed.
She flies it home and stacks it in a cell. Then another. Ten, twelve, up to 25 per cell.
On the first spider she lays one egg. Then she seals the cell with mud.
The larva hatches in the dark and eats through the living pantry, one spider at a time. One nest held over 120.

description:
Mud dauber wasps build tubes of mud, then hunt spiders, sting them into paralysis and stack them alive in each cell, from about 10 to as many as 25 per cell.
The female lays a single egg on the first spider and seals the cell; the larva eats the paralyzed spiders one by one. A twelve-cell nest examined by Mississippi State entomologists held more than 120 spiders.
Worse than the zombie caterpillar? Comment below.
first_comment: The male sometimes stands guard at the nest, because other female wasps will steal the spiders and tiny parasitic wasps try to get at the larvae. Which wasp should we cover next?
